headline: power down 10% on the week to £110/MWh, off the late-July high
commentary: The market has turned over this week. UK power spot is £110.33/MWh, down 4.9% on the day and down about 10% from £122 a week ago. Front-month NBP gas has followed it down to 133 p/therm from 142, though it did bounce 4% today. The more important move is further out the curve: Nov 26, Dec 26 and Jan 27 have each shed 10–12 p/therm in a week, so Jan 27 now prices at 137.5 p/therm against 149.1 a week ago and Winter 26 sits at 133.3 against 143.5. That is the winter risk premium compressing by roughly 8% — the part of the curve that actually sets a renewal price. For anyone renewing into this winter it is a materially better entry than last week. Today's 4% bounce is the reminder that these windows close as quickly as they open: worth fixing the energy block where the term suits rather than waiting for a lower low.

gas.note: NBP front-month is 133.1 p/therm, up 3.95% on the day but down from 142 a week ago and well off the late-July high near 155. The winter curve has come down with it.
